glossary.seoDescription: GourMerge glossary — understand git concepts explained as cooking terms.
glossary.subtitle: Git concepts explained as cooking terms. Git-savvy users will find the technical term in the badge.

recipe.description: A recipe on GourMerge is a full repository: it has a title, ingredients, steps, branches, a commit history, and can be forked.
recipe.helpHint: Recipes work like GitHub repositories. Everything you know about forking, branching, and committing applies here.

fork.description: Create your own independent copy of someone else's recipe to adapt freely.
fork.helpHint: Forking creates a personal copy of a recipe. Your changes stay separate from the original unless you submit a GourMerge Request.

branch.description: A parallel version of your recipe — experiment without changing the main version.
branch.helpHint: Think of a branch as a 'vegan variant' or 'gluten-free version'. Changes on a branch don't affect other branches until you merge.

commit.description: A named snapshot of your recipe at a specific point in time.
commit.helpHint: Every commit saves all ingredients and steps as a snapshot. You can always go back and see exactly what changed.

merge.description: Apply changes from one variant into another, combining the best of both.
merge.helpHint: When you merge, GourMerge combines the ingredient and step changes. If two people changed the same ingredient differently, you'll see a conflict to resolve.

gourmergeRequest.description: Propose your improvements to the original recipe author for review and merging.
gourmergeRequest.helpHint: A GourMerge Request lets you share your recipe improvements with the original author. They can review your changes, leave comments, and merge them into the original.

diff.description: A side-by-side view of exactly what changed between two versions of a recipe.
diff.helpHint: The diff shows added ingredients in green, removed ones in red, and modified ones highlighted. For step text, individual word changes are highlighted.

history.description: A timeline of all saved versions of this recipe, oldest to newest.
history.helpHint: Every time you commit changes, a new entry appears here. Click any commit to see the full recipe at that point in time, or compare it to another version.

conceptIntro.title: Welcome to GourMerge
conceptIntro.subtitle: GourMerge is like GitHub for recipes. Here is a quick overview of what you can do:

recipe.desc: A recipe is a full repository with ingredients, step-by-step instructions, and a complete version history.

fork.desc: Make your own copy of someone else's recipe and adapt it freely — original is unchanged.

branch.desc: Try a variation of your recipe (e.g., vegan version) without touching the main version.

commit.desc: Save a snapshot of your recipe at any point. You can always go back to any earlier version.

merge.desc: Merge changes from one branch into another — GourMerge handles conflicts for you.

gourmergeRequest.desc: Propose your changes to the original recipe's author — they can review, comment, and accept.

explore.title: Discover Recipes
explore.desc: Browse public recipes from the community — filter by difficulty, tags, or sort by popularity.

newRecipe.title: Create a Recipe
newRecipe.desc: Start a new recipe repository. Add ingredients, write step-by-step instructions, and commit your first version.

fork.title: Remix It
fork.desc: Fork any public recipe to make your own copy. Experiment freely — the original stays untouched.

star.title: Star Recipes
star.desc: Star recipes you love. Find them again on your profile page.

history.title: Version History
history.desc: Every commit you make is saved here. Click any version to see the full recipe at that point in time.

gourmergeRequest.title: Propose Changes
gourmergeRequest.desc: Open a GourMerge Request to propose your fork's changes back to the original recipe author.
